title: Exactness of the formal glueing complex
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $f_1,\dots,f_t\in R$ and $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$, such that the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism. For an $R$-module $M$ let $M\otimes_RS$ be its base change [def-weil-module-base-change], $M_{f_i}$, $M_{f_if_j}$ its localizations [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], and identify $(M\otimes_RS)_{f_i}$ with $M_{f_i}\otimes_RS$ canonically. Consider the sequence $0\to M\xrightarrow{\alpha}(M\otimes_RS)\times\prod_iM_{f_i}\xrightarrow{\beta}\prod_i(M\otimes_RS)_{f_i}\times\prod_{i,j}M_{f_if_j}$ with $\alpha(m)=(m\otimes1,m/1,\dots,m/1)$ and $\beta(m',(m_i)_i)=\big((m'/1-m_i\otimes1)_i,(m_i/1-m_j/1)_{i,j}\big)$ (the images of $m_i\in M_{f_i}$, $m_j\in M_{f_j}$ in $M_{f_if_j}$). Then this sequence is exact: $\alpha$ is injective and $\operatorname{Ker}\beta=\operatorname{Im}\alpha$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data, line 24579), the complex (equation-glueing-complex) before it, and its two proofs

proof.text: (Torsion and the localizations.) Let $P$ be an $R$-module and $x\in P$. If $x/1=0$ in $P_{f_i}$ for every $i$, then $f_i^{k_i}x=0$ for some $k_i\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]; with $k=1+\sum_i k_i$, $I^k$ is generated by the monomials $f_1^{a_1}\cdots f_t^{a_t}$ with $\sum a_i=k$, each of which has some $a_i\ge k_i$, so $I^kx=0$ and $x\in P[I^\infty]:=\{x:I^nx=0\text{ for some }n\}$. Conversely if $I^nx=0$ then $f_i^nx=0$, so $x/1=0$ in every $P_{f_i}$. In the same way, if $f_i^nx=0$ for all $i$ then $I^{t(n-1)+1}x=0$ (a monomial of degree $t(n-1)+1$ in $f_1,\dots,f_t$ has some exponent $\ge n$). We apply this to $P=M$ and to $P=M\otimes_RS$ (an $R$-module via $\varphi$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data), second (computational) proof, 'If alpha(m)=0, then m in M[I^infty], see Lemma 05EA' and 'm'' in (M otimes_R S)[(IS)^infty]'; the pigeonhole argument written out

proof.text: (The identification.) Let $\phi:M\to M\otimes_RS$, $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ [def-weil-module-base-change], an $R$-linear map. Its localization $\phi_{f_i}:M_{f_i}\to(M\otimes_RS)_{f_i}$, $x/f_i^e\mapsto(x\otimes1)/f_i^e$, is well defined and $R$-linear [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] (naturality clause). Under the canonical identification $M_{f_i}\otimes_RS=(M\otimes_RS)_{f_i}$, $(x/f_i^e)\otimes s\leftrightarrow(x\otimes s)/f_i^e$, of the statement, the element $m_i\otimes1$ for $m_i\in M_{f_i}$ is $\phi_{f_i}(m_i)$. So $\beta(m',(m_i)_i)=\big((m'/1-\phi_{f_i}(m_i))_i,(m_i/1-m_j/1)_{i,j}\big)$, where $m_i\mapsto m_i/1$ is the canonical map $M_{f_i}\to M_{f_if_j}$, $x/f_i^e\mapsto f_j^ex/(f_if_j)^e$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data), second (computational) proof, the identification (M otimes_R S)_{f_i} = M_{f_i} otimes_R S implicit in the complex (equation-glueing-complex, line 24563)

proof.text: ($\beta\circ\alpha=0$.) For $m\in M$, $\beta(\alpha(m))$ has $i$-th first component $(m\otimes1)/1-\phi_{f_i}(m/1)=(m\otimes1)/1-(m\otimes1)/1=0$ and $(i,j)$-component $m/1-m/1=0$ in $M_{f_if_j}$, since both canonical maps $M_{f_i}\to M_{f_if_j}$, $M_{f_j}\to M_{f_if_j}$ send $m/1$ to $m/1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Hence $\operatorname{Im}\alpha\subseteq\operatorname{Ker}\beta$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data), second (computational) proof, the sequence (equation-glueing-complex) is a complex

proof.text: ($\alpha$ is injective.) Let $\alpha(m)=0$. Then $m/1=0$ in every $M_{f_i}$, so $m\in M[I^\infty]$ by step 1, and $m\otimes1=0$ in $M\otimes_RS$. The ideal $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$ is finitely generated, $\varphi$ is flat and $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism, so the map $M[I^\infty]\to(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-submodule-flat-base-change-iso]; as it sends $m$ to $0$, $m=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data), second (computational) proof, first paragraph; the source deduces m=0 from part (2) of Lemma 05EC (Hom_R(R/I^n,M) = Hom_S(S/I^nS, M otimes S)); here part (1) of 05EC, injectivity on M[I^infty], is used, which gives the same conclusion directly

proof.text: (Normalising an element of the kernel.) Let $(m',(m'_i)_i)\in\operatorname{Ker}\beta$. Write $m'_i=a_i/f_i^{e_i}$ and, with $n_0=\max_ie_i$, $m'_i=f_i^{n_0-e_i}a_i/f_i^{n_0}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. By step 2, $\beta=0$ says: (a) $m'/1=(x_i\otimes1)/f_i^{n_0}$ in $(M\otimes_RS)_{f_i}$, where $x_i=f_i^{n_0-e_i}a_i$, i.e. $f_i^{c}(f_i^{n_0}m'-x_i\otimes1)=0$ in $M\otimes_RS$ for some $c\ge0$; (b) $f_j^{n_0}x_i/(f_if_j)^{n_0}=f_i^{n_0}x_j/(f_if_j)^{n_0}$ in $M_{f_if_j}$, i.e. $(f_if_j)^{c}(f_j^{n_0}x_i-f_i^{n_0}x_j)=0$ in $M$ for some $c$ (definition of equality in a localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]). Take one $c$ for the finitely many conditions, and put $n=n_0+c$, $m_i=f_i^cx_i$. Then $m'_i=m_i/f_i^n$, and (a), (b) become $$f_i^nm'=m_i\otimes1\ \text{in }M\otimes_RS,\qquad f_j^nm_i=f_i^nm_j\ \text{in }M\qquad(1\le i,j\le t).$$ Indeed $f_i^nm'-m_i\otimes1=f_i^c(f_i^{n_0}m'-x_i\otimes1)=0$ and $f_j^nm_i-f_i^nm_j=(f_if_j)^c(f_j^{n_0}x_i-f_i^{n_0}x_j)=0$. Put $g_i=f_i^n$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data), second (computational) proof, second paragraph, 'Write m'_i = m_i/f_i^n ... after possibly enlarging n assume that f_i^n m' = m_i otimes 1 in M otimes_R S and f_j^n m_i - f_i^n m_j = 0 in M'; the enlargement written out

proof.text: (The Koszul group $H_1$ and its annihilator.) For an $R$-module $P$ let $d_P:P^{t}\to P^{t\times t}$, $(x_i)_i\mapsto(g_jx_i-g_ix_j)_{i,j}$, let $Z(P)=\operatorname{Ker}d_P$, let $\delta_P:P\to Z(P)$, $x\mapsto(g_ix)_i$ (it lands in $Z(P)$ since $g_jg_ix-g_ig_jx=0$), and $H(P)=Z(P)/\delta_P(P)$, with quotient map $\pi_P$. For $z=(x_i)\in Z(P)$ and each $k$, $g_kz=(g_kx_i)_i=(g_ix_k)_i=\delta_P(x_k)$, so $g_1,\dots,g_t$ annihilate $H(P)$; by the last remark of step 1, $I^{t(n-1)+1}\subseteq(g_1,\dots,g_t)$, so $H(P)$ is killed by $I^{t(n-1)+1}$, in particular $I$-power torsion. By step 5, $z:=(m_i)_i\in Z(M)$; let $\xi=\pi_M(z)\in H(M)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data), second (computational) proof, 'the element xi of H_1(M,(f_1^n,...,f_t^n))', with H_1 as in Lemma 05EE (lemma-explicit-ext, line 24413), and its annihilation by Lemma 05EF (lemma-koszul-homology-annihilated, line 24454), whose three-line proof is written out here

proof.text: ($\xi=0$.) The sequence $0\to Z(M)\to M^t\xrightarrow{d_M}M^{t\times t}$ is exact, so, $S$ being flat over $R$, $Z(M)\otimes_RS\to M^t\otimes_RS$ is injective [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] (applied with the flat $R$-module $S$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]). Compose with the isomorphism $M^t\otimes_RS\to(M\otimes_RS)^t$, $(x_i)_i\otimes s\mapsto(x_i\otimes s)_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product]; call the injective composite $\iota$. Then $\iota(z\otimes1)=(m_i\otimes1)_i$, and for $y=\sum_l y_l\otimes s_l\in M\otimes_RS$, $\iota((\delta_M\otimes1)(y))=\sum_l(g_iy_l\otimes s_l)_i=(g_iy)_i$. With $y=m'$, step 5 gives $(g_im')_i=(m_i\otimes1)_i$, so $z\otimes1=(\delta_M\otimes1)(m')$ by injectivity of $\iota$. Hence $\xi\otimes1=(\pi_M\otimes1)(z\otimes1)=((\pi_M\circ\delta_M)\otimes1)(m')=0$ in $H(M)\otimes_RS$ [def-weil-module-base-change] (functoriality of $-\otimes_RS$, and $\pi_M\circ\delta_M=0$). Since $H(M)$ is $I$-power torsion (step 6), $\varphi$ is flat and $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism, $H(M)\to H(M)\otimes_RS$, $\eta\mapsto\eta\otimes1$, is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-module-flat-base-change-iso]; so $\xi=0$, i.e. $z\in\delta_M(M)$: there is $m\in M$ with $m_i=g_im=f_i^nm$ for all $i$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data), second (computational) proof, second paragraph, 'since R -> S is flat ... H_1(M,f^n) = H_1(M,f^n) otimes_R S = H_1(M otimes_R S, f^n) by Lemma 05E9 (lemma-neighbourhood-isomorphism). The existence of m' implies that xi maps to zero in the last group, i.e. xi is zero'; only the injectivity of H_1(M) otimes S -> H_1(M otimes S) on the relevant element is needed and is proved here

proof.text: ($\operatorname{Ker}\beta\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\alpha$.) With $m$ from step 7, $m'_i-m/1=f_i^nm/f_i^n-m/1=0$ in $M_{f_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], so $(m',(m'_i)_i)-\alpha(m)=(m'',0,\dots,0)$ with $m''=m'-m\otimes1$. By step 5, $f_i^nm''=m_i\otimes1-f_i^nm\otimes1=0$ for all $i$, so $m''\in(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$ (step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-submodule-flat-base-change-iso] there is $x\in M[I^\infty]$ with $x\otimes1=m''$; by step 1, $x/1=0$ in every $M_{f_i}$, so $\alpha(x)=(m'',0,\dots,0)$. Hence $(m',(m'_i)_i)=\alpha(m+x)\in\operatorname{Im}\alpha$. Together with steps 3 and 4: $\alpha$ is injective and $\operatorname{Ker}\beta=\operatorname{Im}\alpha$.
